approach: Derive the limit in code at dispatch and store it on the job record. `AcceptedReading::allowed_paths()` (briefs.rs) returns the reading's deliverable paths when a criterion matches a narrow, windowed phrase matcher (`limiting_criterion()`), and `None` otherwise. The Job gets an optional `allowed_paths` field set in the literal at run/mod.rs:994, and dispatch prints one `scope` UI line naming the paths and the matching criterion. A path-only helper `outside_allowed_paths(allowed, changed)` sits beside `unchanged_planned_files`, with the same `normal_path` normalisation. It runs at two points. (1) In `producer_loop` (run/producer.rs:162-366), after each report: an outside file joins the one send-back through a new `send_back_text_scoped`, which names each path and the matching criterion and says to revert; a still-outside diff gets one extra scope-only send-back. (2) At the head of `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1544), before the decision gate, CI push and verifier: a still-outside diff, or a resumed candidate that never went through the loop, closes the job as Failed. The reason starts with `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` and names the paths and criterion, and `retry_findings` carries it to a retry's producer. A job with no stored list is never checked. Only Rust, CHANGELOG.md and one row of docs/records.md change; no prompt, governance file or records/ file.

decisions.choice: Derive the allowed list from the accepted reading in code: `AcceptedReading::allowed_paths(&self) -> Option<Vec<String>>` and `limiting_criterion(&self) -> Option<&str>` (briefs.rs). The list is the deliverable paths with a leading `./` removed and duplicates dropped, when some criterion matches `limits_changed_files(text)`. `None` when no criterion matches or the reading has no deliverables.
decisions.reason: The reading says the limit is derived in code from the accepted criteria and deliverables, and the reader prompt has no token headroom. Methods on the existing view add no field to `AcceptedReading`, so its struct literals (send_back.rs:214, reading.rs:5922, run_pin_tests.rs:1047) do not change. An empty list is never stored because it would flag every file.

rejected.option: Add an allowed_paths output field to the reader or to Reading
rejected.why: Out of scope: no new reader output field, no prompt edits.

rejected.option: Use the plan's files plus the deliverables (as planned_paths does)
rejected.why: The limit is the accepted reading's, not the planner's.

rejected.option: Treat any criterion containing 'only' as limiting

decisions.choice: Revised matcher (answers finding 3). `limits_changed_files(text)` lowercases the text and turns every non-alphanumeric run into one space, then matches only these windowed forms: (a) `no file` or `no files` followed, within 8 words, by `outside` and then, within 8 more words, by `changed`, `change`, `changes`, `modified` or `touched`; (b) `no other file(s)` followed within 3 words by `changed`, `change`, `modified` or `touched` (covers 'no other file is changed', 'no other files may change'); (c) `only` followed within 6 words by `may change`, `may be changed` or `may be modified`; (d) the literal `test only` / `tests only` written with a hyphen (`test-only`, `tests-only`), compared before the hyphen is flattened, or the words `test only change|diff|job`; (e) `production` optionally followed by `code`, optionally by `is`/`are`, then `unchanged`. Dropped from round 1: bare `nothing outside`, bare `no other file(s)`, and the open-ended `only ... is/are changed`.
decisions.reason: The critic grepped the repository and found round 1's phrases in prose that limits nothing: docs/design/records-history.md:134 'Content cannot be judged only after the merge, because by then main is changed', docs/design/athena-v0.md:984 'nothing outside the commit is needed', reading.rs:6598 'cites no other file', docs/design/context-engineer.md:153 'facts no other file states'. Each remaining form needs a path word and a change verb together in a short window, so those sentences no longer match. It still covers the request's examples 'no file outside X changed' (a) and 'test-only, production unchanged' (d, e) and the reading's 'only ... may change' (c). A false match is costly, because the list is only the deliverables (this job's own deliverable list omits producer.rs and store.rs), so the rule errs toward not matching. A missed limit only means the verifier catches it, as today.

rejected.why: Matches the quoted repository sentences; a false match closes a correct diff as Failed.

rejected.option: A model call or reader-supplied flag to judge limiting criteria
rejected.why: Not a code check, and needs a new reader field or prompt change.

decisions.choice: Store the list on the Job record as `allowed_paths: Option<Vec<String>>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, set in the Job literal at run/mod.rs:994 and read back through `ctx.job.job` (set at run/mod.rs:1053). Document it in the `athena.job/1` row of docs/records.md:92: 'optional `allowed_paths`, present only when an accepted criterion limits which files may change'.
decisions.reason: This is how `pin` and `dispatch_branch` were added, so older records parse under `deny_unknown_fields`. The same stored list serves a fresh run, a retry and a resumed candidate, which share `ctx`. The 'strangers' default asks that records be described for an outside reader; one clause in an existing row is small enough to include (finding 4). No test reads that table: the only Rust references to docs/records.md are status.rs:1844, 1930 and 1933, which cite section names.

rejected.why: The request says store it with the job; the stored value is auditable.

rejected.why: The new field is cheap to document and the row is the outside reader's only description of the record.

decisions.choice: Make the scope visible to operators (finding 5). At dispatch, right after the `dispatched ...` line (run/mod.rs:1047), when `allowed_paths` is Some, print one line: `scope      allowed paths: a, b (from criterion "…")`. The criterion text comes from `accepted.limiting_criterion()`, which `producer_loop` (param `accepted`, producer.rs:166) and `check_and_verify` (param `accepted`, mod.rs:1547) both hold. The send-back text and the point-2 reason both quote the criterion.
decisions.reason: Without it the first sign of a limited job is a send-back or a Failed close, and deliverable lists can be incomplete. The criterion in the message tells the operator and the next producer why the limit exists.

rejected.why: A second new record field for something recomputable from the accepted reading; the list alone is the requested record.

decisions.choice: Check at two points. (1) `producer_loop`: compute the changed path list once from `changes` (producer.rs:268) outside the `unchanged` block, call `outside_allowed_paths`, add the result to the break condition (producer.rs:290) and to `problems`. It is not added to `report_problems` (producer.rs:315), because the job ends before the verifier. (2) Head of `check_and_verify` (mod.rs:1565): if `recorded_checks.is_none()` and a list is stored, compare `closing.candidate.changes` with it; on a hit call `self.failure` with a reason starting `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX`, restore `changed_paths` and set `verification_passed = None` as the decision branch does (mod.rs:1572-1576), and return before `push_ci_branch` (mod.rs:1583).
decisions.reason: The request asks for the check before hand-off and again before verification. Point 2 stops a diff still outside after the loop's send-backs and a resumed candidate that skipped the loop.

rejected.option: Check only in the producer loop
rejected.why: A diff still outside after the last send-back would reach the verifier.
The producer's working directory is gone there, so it cannot be sent back.

decisions.choice: Give an out-of-scope diff its own extra send-back: `SCOPE_SEND_BACKS = 1`, counted apart from `send_backs` (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` stays 1). The limit test at producer.rs:336 becomes `send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS && !(!outside.is_empty() && scope_send_backs < SCOPE_SEND_BACKS)`. A send-back that has the shared slot free uses it; otherwise the scope slot is used. At most 3 producer runs, only for a job with a stored list.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 asks that an out-of-list change made after the first send-back is sent back again before the verifier; the shared limit of 1 cannot do that. For a job with no list `outside` is empty and the old branch runs.

rejected.option: Raise PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS to 2 for all jobs
rejected.why: Changes unrelated behavior and the tests that pin one send-back (run_pin_tests.rs:1336).

decisions.choice: Add `send_back_text_scoped(brief, unmet, unchanged, replay, gate, scope: Option<(&[String], &str)>)` in send_back.rs, where scope is the outside paths and the criterion. `send_back_text_full` delegates with `None`. With a scope it adds a leading sentence and a section 'Files changed outside the job's allowed paths (revert each):' listing each path as a '- path' line, quoting the criterion, and saying to restore each file to the base content (or delete it if added) and that a file still outside afterwards closes the job before the verifier runs. With `None` the text is byte-for-byte today's.
decisions.reason: Existing signatures and expected texts (send_back.rs ~363-412, run_pin_tests.rs ~1133-1287) stay unchanged.

risks.risk: A phrase match on an innocent criterion stores a list and blocks a legitimate diff, such as producer.rs and store.rs for this very job.
risks.mitigation: The matcher is narrowed to windowed forms that need a path word and a change verb together (decision 2). The tests carry this job's 8 criteria and the four repository sentences from finding 3 as non-matches. A limiting reading with no deliverables stores nothing. The dispatch `scope` line and the criterion quoted in every message make a wrong match easy to diagnose.

risks.risk: `deny_unknown_fields` means an older Athena binary cannot read a job.json that has the new key.
risks.mitigation: The field is optional, skipped when None and defaulted when absent, so existing records parse (new test). It is written only for a limited job.

risks.risk: Changing the loop's send-back limit and break condition alters behavior for jobs with no stored list.
risks.mitigation: Both new inputs are empty for such a job, so the old branches run; the existing send-back tests (run_pin_tests.rs:1336-1387, run/tests.rs:2303-2480) must pass unmodified.

risks.risk: A job closed at the second check has no verification, so its reason might not reach the retry's producer.
risks.mitigation: `retry_findings` accepts `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` (tested), and the reason names each path, the criterion and the fix.

risks.risk: The fake reader's gate may refuse the extra criterion the end-to-end tests add.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core scope_send_back` and adjusts the wrapper only. If the reader's gate refuses the criterion, the producer reports it and does not change the gate.

risks.risk: The deliverable list omits run/producer.rs and store.rs, and docs/records.md is added.
risks.mitigation: The plan names all three with reasons; the producer lists them in its report. The planned-files check flags only planned files left unchanged.

risks.risk: A window in the matcher is too tight or loose and misses a real limiting criterion.
risks.mitigation: A miss only means the job is unchecked, as today, and the verifier still catches it. Each form has a positive unit test, and the windows are constants named in briefs.rs.

Negative cases give `None`: each of this job's 8 criteria, the four repository sentences from finding 3 (records-history.md:134, athena-v0.md:984, reading.rs:6598, context-engineer.md:153), a reading with no limit, and a limiting criterion with no deliverables. An end-to-end test runs an unscoped job whose producer edits README.md and NOTES.md.
demonstrations.observes: The stored list equals the deliverable paths for limiting readings and is None for the rest. The unscoped job has one producer prompt, one verifier run and no scope reason or `scope` UI line.
demonstrations.fails_without: A matcher that ignored criteria returns None for limiting readings and fails the equality. One that matched the repository sentences fails the negative cases, and one that matched everything flags NOTES.md in the unscoped job.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `AcceptedReading::allowed_paths` and `limiting_criterion` (step 1) and `Athena::go`. The pure tests use the existing `accepted()` builder (run_pin_tests.rs:1046) and set deliverables on its public field. The end-to-end test uses the existing `governed_job` helper (run/tests.rs:2252), which takes extra producer edits. No double holds logic under test.

demonstrations.method: End-to-end tests with the scoped wrapper. Test A: the producer edits NOTES.md on attempt 0, a different file EXTRA.md on attempt 1 (after the first send-back), and reverts both on attempt 2. Test B: every attempt edits NOTES.md.
demonstrations.observes: Test A: three producer prompts, prompts[2] contains '## Sent back' and names EXTRA.md, one verifier run. Test B: three producer runs, verifier count 0, the outcome is Failed and its reason starts with `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` and names NOTES.md (point 2). A UI-lines assertion shows the 'files still outside the allowed paths after the send-back' line.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the extra scope allowance, attempt 1 hits the limit at producer.rs:336, so Test A has two producer prompts and the job closes at point 2 with verifier count 0, so the three-prompt assertion fails (finding 6). With no check in `check_and_verify`, Test B reaches the verifier (count 1) with no scope reason.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `Athena::go` → `producer_loop` (point 1) and `check_and_verify` (point 2). The fakes are the existing `editing`/`counting` scripts plus a per-attempt wrapper that picks the edit from the prompt vector, as `reconciling_on_send_back` does (run/tests.rs:2288). The wrapper is added by step 9; `Counts`, `athena_with` and `Lines` exist.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in records.rs. One builds a Job with `allowed_paths: Some(vec!["crates/a.rs","README.md"])` through the `job_on` helper, serialises with `AnyRecord::to_json`, asserts the text contains `"allowed_paths"`, re-parses it and passes the bytes and `canonical_path()` to `check_record_file`. The other uses a Job JSON with no `allowed_paths` key and asserts `check_record_file` returns the record with `allowed_paths == None` and that re-serialising omits the key.
demonstrations.observes: The round-tripped record equals the original; the old-shape record passes the records check.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, the new record fails `deny_unknown_fields` on parse. Without `#[serde(default)]` the old-shape record fails; without `skip_serializing_if` the old-shape text gains the key and the absence assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `check_record_file(path, bytes)` and `AnyRecord::parse`/`to_json`. The fixture is the existing `job_on` helper (records.rs:5118) next to `a_job_keeps_its_dispatch_branch_through_a_round_trip` (records.rs:5137); step 2 adds the field. The seam exists today.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the working-tree diff: only the listed Rust files, store.rs, run/producer.rs, docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md changed; existing tests are unchanged apart from `allowed_paths: None` in Job literals; nothing in athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, prompt files or records/.

demonstrations.method: A pure test calls `send_back_text_scoped` with two outside paths and a criterion, asserts both appear as '- path' lines under the outside-paths heading, that the text quotes the criterion and contains the revert instruction, and that with `None` scope the output equals `send_back_text_full`'s. The CHANGELOG entry is read from the diff.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core scoped_send_back && git diff -- CHANGELOG.md
demonstrations.observes: Each offending path is named and the text says to revert it. CHANGELOG.md shows one new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` naming the stored allowed paths and the two checks.
demonstrations.fails_without: A text that did not list the paths or did not say to revert fails the assertions; no changelog bullet means an empty diff for CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `send_back_text_scoped` (added by step 4), called directly. The changelog check is a diff read. No doubles.

open_questions: User: Is the extra scope-only send-back (up to 3 producer runs for a job with a stored list) wanted? The alternative is the single shared send-back, closing the job at the second check, which saves a producer run but cannot send a second out-of-list change back.

User: Should the stored list also cover files a build always rewrites, such as Cargo.lock, for a limited job? As planned, any changed file outside the deliverables is flagged, which is what the request says.
